concepts.title: Spherical Mirrors: Concave and Convex
concepts.definition: A spherical mirror is a curved slice of a hollow sphere: the inward-bulging reflecting face is concave and converges light, while the outward face is convex and spreads light out; pole, centre of curvature, focus and aperture are the standard points that describe either mirror.
concepts.key_idea: Concave mirrors gather rays to a focus; convex mirrors scatter them as if from behind.
question_patterns: define concave and convex mirrors
name the terms used to describe a spherical mirror
which mirror is used as a dentist's mirror and why
what is the pole of a spherical mirror
why is a convex mirror used in vehicle rear views
how can you identify a concave mirror by touch or trial

solution_steps.explain: Bulging inward marks concave; bulging outward marks convex.
The mirror is part of a sphere, so its pole, centre and radius follow from the sphere.
Concave brings parallel rays to the focus; convex makes them diverge from the focus.

concepts.title: Images Formed by Spherical Mirrors
concepts.definition: A concave mirror gives different images as the object moves: real and inverted when the object is beyond the focus, magnified when close, and a virtual upright enlarged image inside the focus; a convex mirror always gives a small, upright virtual image - useful for a wide rear view.
concepts.key_idea: Move the object, change the image: position decides real-inverted or virtual-erect.
concepts.textbook_ref: hecu110.txt lines 137-240 (characteristics of images formed by spherical mirrors)
question_patterns: what kind of image forms when an object is very close to a concave mirror

state the uses of concave and convex mirrors

solution_steps.explain: Compare the object distance with the focal length of the mirror.
Beyond focus gives real inverted images; inside focus gives virtual erect magnified ones.
Real images can be caught on a screen; virtual ones only appear in the mirror.

concepts.title: Laws of Reflection
concepts.definition: Reflection follows two rules: the incident ray, the reflected ray and the normal at the point of incidence all lie in one plane, and the angle of reflection equals the angle of incidence - both measured from the normal.
concepts.formula: angle of reflection = angle of incidence
concepts.key_idea: Equal angles about the normal, with all three rays in one plane.
concepts.textbook_ref: hecu110.txt lines 240-518 (what are the laws of reflection)
question_patterns: state the two laws of reflection
a ray strikes a mirror at 40 degrees to the normal - find the angle of reflection
what is the normal in reflection of light
verify the second law of reflection with a plane mirror activity
if the angle of incidence is 0 degrees what happens to the ray
why are the angles measured from the normal and not the surface

solution_steps.explain: The normal stands perpendicular to the mirror at the point where the ray strikes.
Incident ray, normal and reflected ray must share one plane - the first law.
Measure both angles from the normal; they come out equal - the second law.

concepts.title: Lenses: Convex and Concave
concepts.definition: A lens is a transparent piece of glass bounded by curved surfaces that refracts light: a convex lens is thicker in the middle and can converge rays to a real focus to act as a magnifier, while a concave lens is thinner in the middle and spreads rays as if from a virtual focus.
concepts.key_idea: Lens bends light by refraction: bulging middle gathers, hollow middle spreads.
question_patterns: what is a lens - name its two types
how does a convex lens behave like a magnifying glass
what is the focus of a convex lens
why is a concave lens called a diverging lens
distinguish a lens from a mirror in what it does to light
give two uses of lenses in daily life

solution_steps.explain: Middle thick means convex; middle thin means concave.
Convex lenses converge parallel rays to the focus; concave lenses diverge them.
Magnifiers, cameras and spectacles exploit these converging or diverging actions.
